requirement:
# REQ-2297: Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code.

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2297

#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
MessagePack generated code is not decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute.

Because it is very hard to write good coverage for generated MessagePack code, it may skew coverage numbers, especially on large projects with a lot of generated code.

#### Describe the solution you'd like
I would like all generated code to be decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute.  I do not feel like a setting is needed, but setting would be fine to have too.

#### Describe alternatives you've considered
There are no alternatives, it is close to impossible to write good coverage for generated code as it covers many edge cases.

#### Additional context

N/A

story.summary: Every generator template (object formatter, string-key formatter, enum, union, resolver, composite resolver) now puts `[global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` on the type it emits. Each attribute sits inside an `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` block. The resolver templates also decorate their nested helper classes (`FormatterCache<T>` and `GetFormatterHelper`). One shared helper, `TransformUtilities`, now writes a line break after `{` for nesting types that have constraints. Without it, `#if` could land mid-line after the brace. The change adds a README note, a new test class with two tests, and 222 regenerated snapshot files.
story.why: Issue 2297 asks for all generated MessagePack code to carry `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`, so generated formatters stop skewing coverage numbers.
touches_beyond_requirement: TransformUtilities.EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces now writes `{\r\n` instead of `{` when the nesting type has constraints. This changes whitespace in generated output for those types and is the likely cause of the odd +5/-1 and +4/-0 snapshot shapes.
The README paragraph says the attribute is unavailable on netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework. That statement looks factually wrong.
The attribute is applied to the user's own `partial` resolver class, not only to fully generated types.
222 expected snapshot files were regenerated to match the new output (S2 reports 7 distinct change shapes).
story.confidence_overview: High that the five templates exercised by the new test emit the attribute inside the guard, and that each .tt matches its .cs (S1). Medium on the composite resolver and the nested helper classes, which only snapshot tests cover and whose names are not in the diff. Medium on the TransformUtilities fix: it looks needed, but no named test targets it. Low confidence that the `#if` guard is justified: as far as I know, ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute exists in netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework 4.0+, so the guard silently drops the feature for those targets.

REQ-2297 ('all generated code to be decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute') is therefore only partly met.

Claim C2 disputed: StringKeyFormatterTemplate.tt (lines 18-20) and StringKeyFormatterTemplate.cs (line 37) guard [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] with '#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK', omitting the attribute on netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework where ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute is available in the BCL, so REQ-2297 is only partly met.

Claim C3 disputed: Two issues: (1) The named tests in CodeCoverageExclusionTests.cs do not actually test EnumTemplate because MyEnum (lines 37-41) is never referenced by any [MessagePackObject] in TestSource, so no enum formatter is generated, while Assert.True(generated.Count >= 5) (line 71) passes because MyUnionMember (line 49) produces a fourth formatter alongside MyObject, MyStringKeyObject, IMyUnion, and GeneratedMessagePackResolver. (2) EnumTemplate.tt (lines 8-10) and EnumTemplate.cs (line 27) guard the attribute with '#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK', omitting it on netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework where ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute exists, only partly meeting REQ-2297.

Claim C4 disputed: UnionTemplate.tt (lines 10-12) and UnionTemplate.cs (line 30) wrap [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] in '#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK', leaving generated union formatters undecorated on netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework targets despite ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute being available on both, so REQ-2297 is only partly met.

Claim C5 disputed: ResolverTemplate.tt (lines 14-16) and ResolverTemplate.cs (line 38) guard [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] with '#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK', omitting it on netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework targets where ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute is available (partly meeting REQ-2297). Also, partial class <Resolver> is not necessarily top-level since line 11 wraps it in EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces.

Claim C6 disputed: ResolverTemplate.tt (lines 31-33, 48-50) and ResolverTemplate.cs (lines 55-57, 67) wrap [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] on FormatterCache<T> and <Resolver>GetFormatterHelper in '#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK', leaving those generated helper types undecorated on netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework where the attribute is available, so REQ-2297 is only partly met.

Claim C7 disputed: CompositeResolverTemplate.tt (lines 7-9, 35-37) and CompositeResolverTemplate.cs (lines 27, 56-58) wrap [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] in '#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK', omitting the attribute on netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework where ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute exists, so REQ-2297 is only partly met.

Claim C9 disputed: In CodeCoverageExclusionTests.cs lines 21-62, TestSource actually defines two int-key [MessagePackObject] classes (MyObject at line 25 and MyUnionMember at line 49), whereas MyEnum (line 37) is never referenced by any [MessagePackObject]. Consequently, no enum formatter is generated for MyEnum, yet Assert.True(generated.Count >= 5) (line 71) passes because MyUnionMemberFormatter supplies the fifth file. C9's description masks that the enum in TestSource produces no generated file.

Claim C10 disputed: C10 cites ExcludeAttributeIsGuardedForTargetsWhereItIsUnavailable (CodeCoverageExclusionTests.cs lines 81-110) against REQ-2297 ('all generated code to be decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute'), but the test enforces the '#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK' guard that prevents generated code from being decorated on netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework where ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute actually exists. Also, lines 84-96 lack a non-empty check on generated, so an empty generator result would pass vacuously.

The `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` guard (repeated in every template) appears unnecessary. As far as I know, ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute exists in netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework 4.0+ and allows class targets. The effect is that libraries targeting netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework, a large share of MessagePack consumers, get no coverage exclusion. That contradicts 'all generated code'.
The README states the attribute is not available for netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework. This appears to be factually incorrect and would mislead users.

The attribute is emitted on the user's `partial` resolver class. ExcludeFromCodeCoverage has AllowMultiple=false, so a user who already wrote `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` on their partial resolver declaration will hit CS0579 (duplicate attribute) after upgrading. The composite resolver has the same issue at CompositeResolverTemplate.tt line 8.
Applying the attribute to a partial class also excludes any hand-written members the user put in their own part of that resolver class from coverage.

The test only checks that each file contains the attribute at least once. It would still pass if nested types or a second type in the file lost the attribute. The test source also does not exercise the composite resolver or formatters nested in user types; those rely only on regenerated snapshots.
This changes generated whitespace for every nesting type with constraints, adding an extra blank line in some formatters. The change is harmless but adds snapshot churn not visible in the samples.

Emitting [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] (which has AllowMultiple = false) directly on 'partial class <Resolver>' (also in ResolverTemplate.cs line 38) causes a breaking compiler error CS0579 ('Duplicate ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute') for any existing user who already placed [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] on their [GeneratedMessagePackResolver] partial class declaration as a workaround, and silently excludes any user-written members in their part of the partial class from code coverage.

Emitting [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] (AllowMultiple = false) on 'partial class <Resolver>' (also in CompositeResolverTemplate.cs line 27) breaks compilation with CS0579 whenever a user has already decorated their [CompositeResolver] partial class with [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage], and excludes any hand-written members in that partial class from code coverage.

All six generator templates (FormatterTemplate.tt:14, StringKeyFormatterTemplate.tt:18, EnumTemplate.tt:8, UnionTemplate.tt:10, ResolverTemplate.tt:14/31/48, CompositeResolverTemplate.tt:7/35) guard [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] with '#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK', suppressing the attribute for all netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework consumers even though parameterless System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute has been in the BCL since .NET Framework 4.0 and .NET Standard 2.0.

RunGeneratorAsync discards both the updated Compilation and generator Diagnostics ('out _, out _'), so the new tests never verify that the generated code compiles without C# errors, and TestSource leaves MyEnum (line 37) unreferenced by any [MessagePackObject] so EnumTemplate is never exercised despite the comment on line 69.
